pr_title: promql/engine: Introduce SelectManager to control execution of .Select requests
pr_body:
Signed-off-by: Kemal Akkoyun This PR attempts to fix https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/6878 Currently, Prometheus executes PromQL “.Select” queries sequentially. Particularly for the remote storages, this implementation wastes CPU cycles while waiting for independent queries. Requirements that gathered from the comments of https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/6878 and https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/pull/6887. #### Requirements * Should NOT use all the available CPU. * Limit concurrency * PromQL should not care about how the querier is implemented, it should always be the same logic. * Should avoid introducing changes to LOCAL storage. * Should avoid spawning goroutines if there is just a single selector. This PR fulfils the requirements listed above by introducing a small component to regulate select requests against querier. It still misses tests and also I'm gonna add benchmarks. P.S: Regarding https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/pull/7089#issuecomment-617132242 after checking out the comments, I decided a design doc might not be needed. ### Benchmarks #### Old

> Only after this we can start discussions if we should specify higher than 1 for local TSDB or not.

Having more than 1 concurrent Select for a given query should not be possible against the local TSDB (even if allowed against remotes), as it makes CPU unpredictable due to causing spikes during the select stage. Right now queries can't use more than 1 core each - if you remove that provisioning CPU is now much harder and in addition query throughput performance will be worse. There's also likely an adverse memory impact.

Keep in mind that Select is the fast part of a query generally, so we'd making life harder for users without gaining them much.

issue_context.title: promql: Add support for .Select calls concurrency.
issue_context.body:
Hi (again) Prometheus family :wave: 

## Proposal

We noticed with @brancz during our investigations on query latency that `Select` calls done by PromQL are done sequentially: 

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/6950331/75368505-c9705e00-58b9-11ea-9313-9a8c126aa819.png)

It appears that those are subqueries required for the main (quite complex) instant query. Looks like they are done sequentially, where in our opinion they could be done concurrently. 
We would like to propose:

* Running independent subqueries in different goroutines.
* Controlled by some `subqueryMaxConcurrency` flag.

Would that make sense or lack of concurrency here is intended?

**Use case. Why is this important?**
* We are just waiting on one subquery to finish to start another independent subquery. We just waste time, CPU / Resources. We could do those asynchronously.  

cc @roidelapluie @slrtbtfs @brian-brazil @beorn7

It's more that noone brought it up yet. This is also nothing to do with subqueries, you're talking about selectors.

The one thing to watch for is needlessly spawning goroutines, we never need this for local storage for example. A traffic spike to a remote system could also cause it issues.

Yes, that's why something like max concurrency flag maybe make sense?
